title: Review and merge branch utility-usage (fb9bb81): a 'utility' room usage
description: Branch utility-usage, commit fb9bb81, local, not pushed. Adds a 'utility' usage (laundries, plant and store rooms): ROOM_TYPES in __init__.py, _VALID_USAGES in web/server.py, the editor usage list + colour, the URL-fragment codec (char 'u'; existing links still decode), and utility-space / utility-floor entries beside the kitchen ones in share/traces.yml, share/hulls.yml and their simple/ variants -- without the trace entries a utility cell gets no IfcSpace. Behaviour agreed with the owner 2026-10-05: kitchen-style windows; outside door where there is access; reachable from neighbouring rooms like a kitchen (no change to the bedroom/toilet door rule in topologist/graph.py); not a private usage. Why: homemaker-layout's programmes declare usage 'utility' on 18 rooms, which AllocateCells would otherwise silently make 'living'. Tests: tests/test_utility_usage.py (3, all fail without the change); suite 176 passed, server validation 70 (fastapi needed). NOT run: the JS vitest suite (node not installed on the machine that made it). Migrated from homemaker-layout homemaker-py-9zvw.

title: rooms2ifc.py: build an IFC from a rooms document file; move rooms_to_faces_and_widgets into the library
description: homemaker-layout now writes evolved buildings as this repo's web-editor rooms document (rooms.json: vertices, elevation, height, face_styles, usage, plus ignored tracing keys dom_id/code/meta) -- its docs/rooms-format.md. The web editor loads these files already. Wanted: a CLI beside dxf2ifc.py -- rooms2ifc.py rooms.json out.ifc -- calling rooms_to_faces_and_widgets() then Molior.from_faces_and_widgets(). That function lives in web/geometry_adapter.py today; moving it into the library (beside molior) lets the server and the CLI share one copy. Verified 2026-10-05 that the path works end to end on an evolved layout: 11 rooms -> 11 IfcSpaces, walls, windows, doors, roofs in 6 s; and that a wall split by a collinear vertex into party (blank) and street (default) parts keeps both styles (window on the street part only). Paired with homemaker-layout homemaker-py-8b2u.5.

title: Accept roof geometry alongside rooms: rooms + faces together, and faces with any vertex count
description: A 'rooms' cell is a prism (vertical walls, flat floor/ceiling), so pitched roofs cannot be expressed as rooms. Here a roof is a VOID cell enclosed by sloping faces (topologist GetHulls turns non-vertical, non-horizontal faces into roof hulls). homemaker-layout will generate pitched roof geometry for its evolved buildings (Urb's Perl made pitched roofs as Boolean solids: hips from the roof outline, gables on party edges) and needs to hand it over with the rooms. Today GenerateRequest accepts rooms XOR faces (val_not_empty), and FaceData requires exactly 4 vertices, ruling out triangular hip ends. Needed: rooms and faces in one request/document, faces of 3+ vertices, and a widget (void) for the roof cell. A file reader (see the rooms2ifc bead) can take the mix before the server does. Paired with homemaker-layout homemaker-py-6e5u (roof geometry generation).

title: web/geometry_adapter._snap rounds each vertex to 1 mm, breaking T-junctions on non-axis-aligned input
description: _snap (added with the web editor, 28210d5, 2026-05-20, 'to ensure face adjacency within tolerance') rounds every coordinate independently to 3 dp. For editor input (axis-aligned, snapped vertices) it merges float noise on shared walls. For exact geometry at an angle it moves a T-junction corner -- a room corner lying part-way along a neighbour's wall -- off that wall: CellComplex.ByFaces then makes a sliver cell and ApplyDictionary stalls in FaceUtility.InternalVertex. Measured 2026-10-05 on an evolved homemaker-layout plan 75 degrees off the world axes: 12 cells from 11 rooms, build unfinished after 15 minutes; the same rooms rotated to axis-aligned: 11 cells, 7 s. Not the URL fragment's rounding (fragment.js r2, 2 dp, for compact links). Options: drop _snap and rely on ByFaces' 1e-4 tolerance; or cluster near-coincident vertices instead of rounding to a grid. homemaker-layout sidesteps it by exporting axis-aligned frame coordinates, so it is not blocking there. Migrated from homemaker-layout homemaker-py-ejbw.

title: Implement stairs for any cell shape (molior/stair.py is a stub)
description: molior/stair.py: Stair.execute() is 'pass' ('entire stair drawing module still needs porting from Perl Molior library'); share/traces.yml: 'FIXME stairs are not implemented yet'. So no input produces an IfcStair. Owner, 2026-10-05: stairs need implementing; the old Perl only handled quad spaces, but this code can cope with other shapes -- so a NEW implementation for arbitrary convex stair cells, not a port of the quad-only fitter. Inputs that already work: cells with usage 'stair' stacked on consecutive storeys; molior/floor.py already leaves the stairwell open between them. Context: homemaker-layout exports its evolved buildings' stair shafts as such cells (its rooms exporter), and its scorer has its own stair model (graph.stack_corners_in_use, _stair_fit) -- the flight fitter should agree with it on which cells can hold a stair. First seen in homemaker-layout's first end-to-end IFC build (its DESIGN.md §39.91). Migrated from homemaker-layout homemaker-py-eog4.

title: Write A Pattern Language scores to IfcSpace psets for all patterns
description: Pattern assessor scores should be attached to IfcSpace entities as property sets, regardless of whether a HUD overlay exists. The 'light on two sides' pattern already does this and is the reference implementation. All other pattern assessors should follow the same approach, writing their scores to the relevant space psets during IFC generation.
close_reason: All 11 pattern assessors now run in Space.execute() and scores written to EPset_Pattern. SPT stored in Molior and passed to Space. Color coding uses P159 score.

title: Display A Pattern Language scores as HUD overlay in web tool
description: Pattern scores (from Alexander Pattern Language assessors) should be surfaced as a heads-up display overlay in the web viewer. Design questions to resolve before implementing: (1) Are scores merged/averaged for the whole building, or shown per-space? Likely both: per-space from psets, building-level summary in the HUD. (2) Is feedback instant (recomputed on every geometry change) or deferred until IFC generation? Instant is more useful but may be expensive. The HUD could show a simple score list (pattern name + pass/fail or numeric score) updated whenever the model regenerates.

title: Implement Alexander Pattern Language fitness assessors
description: Implement topologic-model fitness assessors for buildable APL patterns. Each assessor evaluates a single cell against a pattern using cell geometry, usage, adjacency, and circulation data. Start with patterns 105, 107, 127, 128, 129, 131, 133, 138, 145, 190.
close_reason: Implemented 10 APL fitness assessors; tests cover both minimal and full-building fixtures; pushed

title: IFC spaces rendered as solid colour — should be hidden or 10% opacity
description: IfcSpace volumes appear as solid coloured masses in the viewer overlay. They should either be fully hidden or rendered at ~10% opacity so they don't obscure the building geometry.
close_reason: removeContextGeometry now strips 'Reference' subcontext, hiding stashed topology tessellation; download still gets original unstripped IFC

title: Vertical edge drag should snap to other vertical edges, not just face planes
description: When dragging a vertical (corner) edge, snapping only considers planes of faces. It should also detect and prioritise alignment with other vertical edges in the scene.

title: Cell drag: prioritise snapping when a cell edge aligns with scene edges
description: Dragging a cell snaps to planes nicely, but when one of the cell's edges aligns with edges already in the scene those shared-edge positions should be prioritised over generic plane snaps.

title: Face drag should snap to all scene edges that intersect the drag plane
description: When dragging a face, snapping currently only considers the dragged cell's own geometry. It should check all edges in the scene for intersection with the drag plane and snap to those too.

title: Cell can be dragged outside the view grid and becomes unretrievable
description: There is no boundary check on drag. A cell dragged past the edge of the visible grid disappears and cannot be selected or recovered without a reset.

title: Clicking cell doesn't select it — only dragging works, which moves the cell
description: Clicking the generated model or a cell in the editor should expose the properties panel/controls without moving anything. Currently the only way to select is to drag, but that immediately starts a move.

title: Increase snap indicator thickness when dragging in web tool
description: When dragging a vertex/face with snap active, the highlighted plane or edge that the snap target is shown on is not visible enough. It should be approximately double the current line thickness (or similar) to make it clear which axis/plane is active during the snap operation.

title: Encode building design as shareable #fragment URL
description:
## Why

Users should be able to bookmark and share a building design without any server-side storage. The natural mechanism is the URL hash fragment (#), which is never sent to the server and can be pasted or linked freely.

## What needs to happen

1. When the room layout changes, serialise it into a compact string and set window.location.hash.
2. On page load, if a hash is present, parse it and restore the layout (instead of or before loading from localStorage).
3. The share/bookmark experience: copy the URL from the browser address bar.

## Encoding strategy — keeping it short

### Step 1: compact JSON schema (before compression)

Replace the verbose editor format with a minimal schema that omits all defaults:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "s": ["foxhouse"],           // only non-default styles used; index → name
  "r": [
    // each room: [vertices_flat, elev?, height?, usage_char?, style_idx?, face_style_idxs?]
    // trailing defaults dropped; coordinates rounded to 2dp (cm precision)
    [[0,0, 4,0, 4,4, 0,4]],                      // elev=0, h=3, usage=l, style=default → all omitted
    [[4,0, 7,0, 7,3, 4,3], 0, 2.4, "b"],          // non-default height and usage
    [[0,4, 4,4, 4,8, 0,8], 0, 3, "l", 1, [1,1,0,0,1,1]]  // per-face styles
  ]
}
```

Usage chars: l=living b=bedroom k=kitchen c=circulation t=toilet s=stair v=void o=outside

### Step 2: deflate-raw + base64url

Use the browser-native CompressionStream API (no library needed, supported everywhere modern):

```js
async function encode(rooms) { ... }  // → URL-safe string, no % encoding needed
async function decode(fragment) { ... }  // → rooms array
```

base64url (RFC 4648 §5) uses A–Z a–z 0–9 - _ so it is safe to put directly after # without percent-encoding.

### Rough size estimate

A 4-room building in the compact schema is ~100–150 bytes of JSON. After deflate-raw: ~80–120 bytes. After base64url: ~110–160 chars. Manageable. A 20-room building: maybe 400–500 chars — long but shareable.

### Fragment format

```
#v1:BASE64URL_OF_DEFLATED_COMPACT_JSON
```

The v1: prefix reserves space for future format changes without breaking old links.

### What NOT to do

- Don't use LZ-string (extra dependency, non-standard).
- Don't gzip (adds 18-byte header overhead that hurts small payloads; deflate-raw is better here).
- Don't base64-standard (+ and / need percent-encoding in URLs).
- Don't skip compression (even small payloads compress 30–50%).

## Acceptance criteria

- Round-trip: encode then decode produces identical room data.
- A 4-room building URL fits in ~200 chars.
- Pasting the URL into a new tab restores the exact layout.
- localStorage still works as a fallback when no hash is present.
- Hash updates are debounced so they don't fire on every pointermove.

title: web/README.md example uses stylename 'party', which is not a share/ style ('blank' is)
description: The /api/generate example in web/README.md uses face style 'party' for a party wall, but share/ has no 'party' directory; the party-wall style that exists, and that Urb's tools used, is 'blank'. Fix the example (and the prose that says party walls get a different stylename). Found 2026-10-05 while writing homemaker-layout's rooms exporter.
